name: the first state is where the node starts: every value jumps to it, State and the At ports are set, and State Changed does NOT fire
because: states.ts :277-289 the list arriving queues the first state; :765-768 → jumpToState :580-616 (:601-613 no State Changed on the first)

name: a later move animates a number on the default curve (ease-out, 300 ms): State and State Changed at once, Done after, the value moves on later frames and Has Reached fires when it lands
because: states.ts :769-850 (:791-797 the default curve, :824-829 start, :849 Done); timerscheduler.ts :177-194 join + onRunning(0), :130-174 run and finish; :255-258 onFinish

name: Toggle moves to the next state and wraps round after the last; with transitions off every move lands at once and Has Reached fires with it
because: states.ts :333-357 Toggle; :359-369 Use Transitions; :799-808 set at once; :839-843 Has Reached when nothing animates

name: asking for the state the node is in is Unchanged; asking twice in a frame for where it is heading is Unchanged at once and queues nothing
because: states.ts :672-680 the pending target; :749-754 already there

name: a state the node does not have: it stays where it is, Error names the states and the nearest one, and the invocation is a Failure (states/unknown-state)
because: states.ts :756-762, :708-741 (nearest-name.ts: equal ignoring case wins outright); :465 any `to-<name>` is accepted

name: a state that does not exist arriving on State (nobody invoked it) pulses Failure bare — no outcome
because: states.ts :485-488 the setter route carries no token; :736-740 the bare pulse

name: with no States at all, Toggle fails at once (states/no-states) and To <state> fails at the frame's end; a State value is dropped silently
because: states.ts :339-345, :634-639; :744-747 no list → the invocation fails, a setter's request is dropped

name: A → B → A inside one frame: the state passed through is settled and reports (State Changed, Has Reached B, Done), and only the last move animates
because: states.ts :617-632, :688-698 the queue; :804 settleImmediately; NDA-002 §4

name: text, true/false and text-style values are set at once on a move, never animated; a true/false the state does not name is false
because: states.ts :779-788

name: a text a state does not name is sent as empty text on every move into it, the first entry too, and the first state publishes a false as false (v4; was D19: the first entry left both as 0, and a move back left the previous state's text on the wire)
because: states.ts typedStateValue, read by jumpToState and goToState alike; ruled 2026-10-02 (P109 ISL-002 §5): the first state sends the typed value; ruled 2026-10-05 (P107-D19, "Send empty text"): a text the state leaves empty is the empty text

name: the first state's empty text arrives as the empty text, and a true/false it names as 1 arrives as true (ISL-002)
because: states.ts typedStateValue: a text is published as the state names it, a true/false is `!!value`

name: a colour transitions per channel, floored, as #rrggbbaa, and lands on the value its state names (a token's own fallback is read; the document has none)
because: states.ts :179-193 onStart, :241-249 the tween, :222-235 lands on the authored value (GAM-006 (b)); color-reader.ts :57-67

name: a colour the reader cannot read (red, an undefined token, transparent is read as no alpha) holds the colour on screen until the end, then lands
because: states.ts :188-192, :205-221 holding, :101-105 transparent; P88 R7 — no page to ask, nothing is reported

name: a curve of 0 ms with no delay is a jump; a value's own curve beats the state's Default; a delay holds the value until it passes
because: states.ts :791-797 own curve, then Default; :800 0 ms and no delay; :205-206 holding before the delay; :813-814 the run is the longest dur + delay

name: a negative delay starts the run in the past: nothing at the join, the next frame is already part-way
because: states.ts :813 Math.min(delay, c.delay); timerscheduler.ts :180 start = now + delay, :185 onRunning(0) only for a delay of exactly 0, :132 the next frame

name: a new move mid-run restarts from wherever the value is, and the interrupted run never reaches
because: states.ts :777 the start values are the values on screen; timerscheduler.ts :43-57 start stops a running timer, a stopped one never finishes

name: a move that animates nothing stops a run still going: the value lands on the new state's at once and stays there, and Has Reached fires once (v3; was row C22: the old run carried on and landed the PREVIOUS state's target)
because: states.ts goToState: every move after the first stops the running timer before it sets values, as jumpToState does; ruled 2026-10-05 (P107-C22, "Stop the running animation"). Before, the timer was only (re)started when something animated, so the old run kept writing B's target and its Has Reached fired a second time

name: a value's input written while the node is in that state reaches the output at once; in another state it waits for the move
because: states.ts :501-509

name: State drives the machine; the old Start State input still moves it, and the States list arriving moves a node that is in no state to it
because: states.ts :474-488; :284 `startState || states[0]` when the list arrives and the node is in no state

name: a State value that arrives BEFORE the States list is overruled by it: the list queues the first state after, and the node ends there
because: states.ts :485-488 queues B; :284 the list arriving finds no state and queues A after it; :688-698 B is passed through, A is where it ends

name: a transition that is not a curve (no `curve`) reads as the state's Default — here the built-in ease-out over 300 ms, since B has none (v2; was row C21: the move threw inside the frame-end callback, the state did not move and no outcome was reported)
because: bezier-easing refuses anything but four finite numbers with both x in [0, 1]; v2 reads such a transition as the state's Default, else the built-in one

name: a refused value transition takes the state's own Default when that one is readable: y moves over B's Default (100 ms, linear), not the built-in 300 ms (v2, C21)
because: v2: a refused `transition-<state>-<value>` reads as `transitiondef-<state>` when that is a curve the library accepts (or sets at once)

name: a refused Default reads as the built-in ease-out over 300 ms (v2, C21)
because: v2: when the refused transition IS the state's Default, the built-in one is used

name: a value input for a name not in Values, written while in its state: the spec keeps it for a later Values list and sends nothing; the runtime throws
because: NSP-020 s82 — P107-S82-STATESVALUEPORT: states.ts :534-541 flags the output `x` without asking whether the node has it, and node.ts throws for a port it does not. The padding the spec carried until s82 registered `x` at mount on the runtime target, so this never reached a play. Known on the runtime until P109 fixes it (R16)

name: R35: an unknown state warns the editor, a second one replaces the sentence, and asking for the state the node is already in clears it — the commonest correction
because: states.ts :786 raises `states/unknown-state` on the error bus, which the editor shows under that key (runtimeerror.ts :177-186); :722-724 withdraw it when a request names a state in the list, before the already-there check, so a request that moves nothing still clears it (v5)

name: R35: a value named as one of the node's own outputs is refused and the editor is told; the sentence stays after the name is changed
because: states.ts :349-355 raise `states/reserved-port-name` for each reserved name in the Values list, the last one's sentence showing; nothing withdraws it (v5)

name: R35: Toggle and To on a one-state node are Unchanged; one that names the state clears an unknown-state sentence, and one with nothing to clear leaves every other sentence standing
because: states.ts :722-724 clear before the :733-736 already-there return, so an Unchanged request withdraws the unknown-state sentence; the reserved-name one (:349-355) is never withdrawn (v5). Kills the two swap-branch mutants seed 20739 left (an Unchanged that clears vs one that does not)

name: R35: a Toggle that moves clears an unknown-state sentence as it is asked, not when the move lands
because: states.ts :722-724 run in `scheduleGoToState`, before the request is queued (v5). Fixes the example the runner swaps into an Unchanged Toggle, so that mutant is killed on every seed (20740 found it by luck of the generated sequences)

name: To Last then To First in one frame, ending at its frame end: the node passes through Last and comes back, so State ends where it began and only State Changed ×2 and the two Dones are seen
because: Shows the declared equivalent for States' frame end (equivalent-mutants.ts: a dropped frame-end `set` shows only at the NEXT settle) on every seed. No generated sequence can draw `to-First` / `to-Last`, no other scenario asks for them, and this play ends at that frame end. Until v5, seed 13 showed it only on frame ends that raised a failure; v5's warnings made those visible at once, and the package test reads a declaration that fires 0 times as dead
